first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. These are directionally aligned symptoms pointing to friction in early user workflows. Memory_31 showed signup simplification lifted first-week activation durably; memory_86 showed shortening onboarding improved completion rates and adoption. Both memories document established effects on the exact metrics we're seeing decline. Activat ion_messaging (memory_91) is a secondary lever but onboarding simplification addresses root friction earlier in the funnel. While promotional_pricing would defend against the competitor's SMB encroachment, it risks margin compression and doesn't address the underlying activation/completion declines—those declines exist independent of competitive pressure and suggest product-side opportunity. A simplified onboarding experiment is lower risk to brand/margin, leverages validated prior learning, and targets the causal friction rather than symptomatic response. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive don't address the current performance headwinds. Pulling memory_31 and memory_86 to verify cohort stability, effect sizes, and implementation details before rolling out at standard_experiment scale.
